rules.when: Trivial or mechanical work whose outcome is fully specified: a rote rename, formatting sweep, typo fix, config or selection flip, deleting or moving named files and sections, removing leftovers a tool generated, or gathering files; multi-file is fine as long as no design choice is left to make.

Well-scoped small implementation work expected to change about 150 lines or fewer: a clearly specified feature, an ordinary bug fix with a clear pointer to the cause, writing tests for existing behavior, or a routine refactor following an existing pattern.

Well-scoped large implementation work expected to change more than about 150 lines: a clearly specified feature, an ordinary bug fix with a clear pointer to the cause, writing tests for existing behavior, or a routine refactor following an existing pattern at that size.
Big or ambiguous multi-file feature, risky refactor, orchestration of several workers, or implementation work that requires holding many moving parts in mind.

Bounded investigation, audit, diagnosis, triage, reproduction, or planning that produces a report rather than a code change: a scout, a survey of issues, a root-cause hunt, an evaluation of options. An ambiguous or cross-system investigation takes the stronger rule below instead.
Ambiguous or cross-system investigation, audit, diagnosis, or planning that spans systems or leaves the scope open.
